title: Rabbi Chalafta (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: One of the five sons of Rabbi Yose, as stated explicitly in the [Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Yevamot](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.1.1.6), and [Shabbat 118b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.118b.9): Rabbi Yose performed levirate marriage with the wife of his brother who had died, and she bore him five sons. In Midrash Tehillim 100:2: “Rabbi Simon and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of Rabbi Chalafta” (Hyman suggests that this may be the same Rabbi Chalafta): “A mortal king, when [a person] confesses, gives him to the executioner — but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so,” etc. Yuchasin wrote that he died in his father’s lifetime, from Semachot, chapter 10, but Hyman does not find it there; in [Moed Katan 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.21a.7) only an incident is mentioned in which Rabbi Yose’s son died in Tzippori, and his name is not mentioned. In the entry Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta Hyman explains that he was the son of this Rabbi Chalafta.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The levirate-marriage account appears in the Yerushalmi. Shabbat gives a list of five sons including Chalafta. In [the consulted Midrash Tehillim](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.100.1), the homily naming Chalafta is in the first digital section of Psalm 100. Hyman gives 100:2.

[Heilprin’s Chalafta notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1326&lang=en) says he died in his father’s lifetime. Moed Katan leaves the son unnamed. Hyman gives Yuchasin’s source claim and says he did not find it in Semachot.
